Job Summary:

The carbon scientist manages agronomic research and scientific analysis; supports greenhouse gas (GHG) accounting, modelling, regenerative ag practice research and implementation, and Sales and Grower Success Team (GST) technical support. This role bridges applied agronomy, data-driven scientific and carbon program development; supporting carbon market integrity, agronomic and carbon performance of regenerative practices, and program outcomes.

Key Responsibilities:

Agronomic Support

  • Provide cross-functional agronomic support and guidance across all teams, ensuring alignment between Science, Data, Modeling, Carbon, GST and Commercial teams. Translate basic and applied research into clear program guidelines, continuous improvements and scalable practice guidance to improve our carbon output
  • Provide technical expertise in range and pasture management, including grazing systems, forage management, soil health, and regenerative grazing practices. Apply this knowledge to support program development, practice guidelines, field implementation, modeling, and carbon outcomes. Candidates with demonstrated experience in range and pasture management are preferred; strong agronomic candidates with the potential and interest to develop into a subject-matter expert in this area will also be considered.
  • Proactively evaluate emerging agronomic practices, technologies, and systems to develop new practice offerings that increase carbon sequestration rates, emissions reductions, and program scalability
  • Lead ongoing evaluation and improvement of agronomic practice guidelines using scientific evidence, field performance data, and modeling insights to maximize carbon yield and credit integrity
  • Continuously working with GST to monitor practice-level data quality, completeness, and consistency, applying agronomic science to identify gaps, risks, or biases and drive improvements in data standards and field-level reporting
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to GST, ensuring training, field visits, and educational resources are scientifically rigorous, practice-aligned, and support carbon credit outcomes
  • Work closely with the modeling team to translate field-level agronomic data into reliable model inputs, proactively addressing data challenges and improving alignment between practice implementation and modeled outcomes
  • Partner with Carbon team and provide agronomic leadership to analyze and resolve Validation and Verification Body (VVB) and Verra findings, including issues related to practice eligibility, data quality, modeling inputs, and scientific justification

Research, Data & Technical Leadership

  • Act as a knowledge hub by regularly updating the company on advances in regenerative agriculture science and technology, fostering continuous learning and improved agronomic decision-making
  • Integrate agronomic science with data analytics, visualization, and reporting to support business success. Support effective communication of complex agronomic and sustainability concepts to farmers, ranchers, and industry partners
  • Attend agronomy and regenerative agriculture conferences to engage with industry experts, identify innovations, and communicate the organization’s scientific achievements
  • Lead preparation of scientific reviews, reports, and white papers based on project outcomes to inform strategy, program development, and external communications.

Background and Training Requirements

  • Education: M.S. or Ph.D. in Soil Science, Rangeland Management, Environmental Science, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
  • Experience: 5+ years of relevant experience in agronomy, regenerative agriculture, agricultural research, soil health, carbon programs, or a related field, with demonstrated ability to lead technical projects and work cross-functionally.
  • Range & Pasture Management: Strong experience in range and pasture management, including grazing systems, forage management, soil health, and regenerative grazing. Candidates with strong agronomic expertise and demonstrated potential to develop into a subject-matter expert in range and pasture systems will also be considered.
  • Carbon & GHG: Working knowledge of agricultural carbon markets, GHG accounting, carbon sequestration, and carbon-credit methodologies. Experience with Verra VCS and VVB processes is highly desirable.
  • Scientific & Analytical Skills: Strong background in applied agronomic research, experimental design, data analysis, scientific interpretation, and translating research into practical field and program recommendations.
  • Modeling & Data: Experience working with agricultural or carbon datasets and models, with the ability to translate field-level information into reliable model inputs and insights.
  • Communication & Leadership: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex science into practical guidance for growers, ranchers, field teams, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Industry Engagement: Demonstrated ability to stay current with regenerative agriculture and carbon science and represent the organization through technical reports, conferences, presentations, and external engagement.
  • Travel: Approximately 20–30% travel required for field visits, grower and rancher engagement, conferences, research activities, and team meetings

Senior Quality Manager

Location: Tanzania, Uganda or Malawi (preferred); India or South Africa considered
Employment type: Full time · Regular travel to project sites
Reports to: Global Head of Carbon Integrity
Manages: Country QA Managers and data validation teams

About Bridge Carbon
Bridge Carbon develops high-integrity carbon projects across Africa and Asia, delivering measurable climate impact while improving lives and strengthening communities. Quality, accuracy and integrity are at the heart of everything we do.

The Role
We are seeking an experienced Senior Quality Manager to set and maintain high quality standards across our carbon project portfolio. You will design, build and own Bridge Carbon's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring every project is delivered in line with clear Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), ISO-aligned quality and risk management principles, and Lean continuous-improvement practices.

You will lead our Country QA Managers and data validation teams, and work closely with the Senior Carbon Integrity Manager (monitoring, reporting, validation and verification) and the Senior Carbon Operations Manager (project piloting, implementation and community engagement) to embed quality across every carbon activity.

Key Responsibilities

Quality Control Strategy & Systems

  • Define and own the quality control strategy, including data and documentation quality
    • Design, implement and maintain a robust QMS, drawing on input from legal, compliance, finance and carbon operations teams
    • Own non-conformance, corrective and preventive action (CAPA) and management review processes
    • Establish document management systems, templates and processes so every carbon project maintains auditable documentation
    • Ensure all project activity is governed by clear, auditable SOPs across the full delivery life cycle
    • Define and embed data quality standards with the IT/Data team, including QA/QC, validation rules, uncertainty management, auditability and traceability
    • Support the development of data collection tools that capture high-quality field data
    • Work with country QA leads to embed quality standards in daily project activities

Internal Quality Audits

  • Establish an internal audit framework and SOP in collaboration with carbon, compliance and legal teams
    • Lead a risk-based internal audit calendar against SOPs, carbon standards and methodologies, and data integrity requirements
    • Audit field data collection, QA/QC procedures and partner compliance, including environmental and social safeguards
    • Introduce spot checks to keep documentation complete and up to date
    • Build a culture of continuous audit readiness, not dependent on verification cycles
    • Track non-conformities and ensure timely root-cause analysis and closure of findings

Continuous Improvement

  • Build a culture of continuous improvement across the quality team
    • Establish standard quality metrics across the portfolio
    • Use audit outcomes and lessons learned to improve SOPs and reduce rework and verification delays
    • Lead initiatives that drive operational excellence, including training and performance tracking

Data Collection & Reporting

  • Gather survey requirements across carbon operations and develop field survey instruments with the IT team
    • Own internal carbon operations tracking and reporting against key objectives and results

What We're Looking For
• Bachelor's degree in environmental science, engineering, sustainability, quality management or a related field, or equivalent practical experience (Master's degree preferred)
• Formal quality qualification such as ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or Implementer (advantageous)
• Proven experience auditing against recognised carbon standards (e.g. Verra, Gold Standard) and working with validation and verification bodies (VVBs)
• A track record of building or substantially improving a QMS, including SOP design, document control and CAPA processes
• Strong working knowledge of ISO 9001 principles and Lean or continuous-

improvement methods

  • Experience leading distributed, multi-country teams
    • Experience in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment

• Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills

Key Attributes
• Brings structure to complex, ambiguous situations and turns quality principles into practical processes
• Breaks complex work into clear milestones, owners and dependencies, and holds people accountable fairly
• Builds trust and gets things done across functions and through people they don't directly manage
• Develops people intentionally, with clear feedback and room to grow
• Communicates clearly and concisely with stakeholders at all levels
• Has high emotional intelligence, strong integrity and a commitment to accuracy and analytical rigour

Why Join Us
This is a rare opportunity to build the quality foundation for a growing portfolio of high-impact climate projects, working with passionate teams across Africa and Asia.

We are looking for a Carbon Analyst responsible for collecting, analysing and reporting carbon emissions data, preparing carbon calculations, supporting client reporting and assisting with wider sustainability projects.

Initially, the role will focus on handling the time-consuming data collection and reporting work that underpins client projects, allowing the consultant to focus on business development and client relationships.

Over time, the successful candidate will become an integral member of the team and take ownership of increasingly complex sustainability reporting.

Key Responsibilities

  • Carbon Accounting & Reporting
  • Collect, review and organise client energy, gas and utility data.
  • Analyse electricity, gas and fuel invoices across multiple client sites.
  • Calculate Scope 1, Scope 2 and relevant Scope 3 emissions.
  • Prepare carbon footprint calculations.
  • Assist in producing Carbon Reduction Plans.
  • Support carbon reporting for clients across a range of industries.
  • Ensure all calculations are accurate and compliant with recognised reporting standards.
  • Maintain detailed audit trails and supporting documentation.
  • Sustainability Support
  • Assist with sustainability reporting and documentation.
  • Research sustainability legislation and compliance requirements.
  • Support ESG and environmental reporting projects.
  • Prepare client reports and presentation material.
  • Monitor regulatory and compliance updates.
  • Assist with sustainability data collection and verification.
  • Data Management
  • Extract information from utility bills, invoices and spreadsheets.
  • Maintain accurate emissions databases.
  • Perform quality assurance checks on data.
  • Organise large volumes of client information.
  • Identify missing or inconsistent data.
  • Maintain structured project files and documentation.
  • Business Support
  • Prepare proposal support documentation.
  • Assist with research for client projects.
  • Produce charts, summaries and reports.
  • Support process improvement initiatives.
  • Help automate reporting workflows using AI where appropriate.

Requirements

Essential Skills & Experience

  • Experience working with sustainability, ESG or environmental reporting.
  • Experience preparing carbon calculations or emissions reporting.
  • Strong analytical skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • Advanced Excel skills.
  • Comfortable working with large datasets.
  • Ability to interpret utility invoices and consumption data.
  • Strong written English.
  • Excellent organisational skills.
  • Ability to work independently.
  • High level of accuracy.

Highly Desirable

  • Experience with Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol.
  • Knowledge of Carbon Reduction Plans (CRPs).
  • Experience with Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions.
  • Understanding of UK sustainability legislation.
  • Experience preparing SECR, PPN 06/21 or similar reporting.
  • Knowledge of ISO 14064 or ISO 14001.
  • Experience using Power BI or similar reporting tools.
  • Experience using AI tools such as ChatGPT to improve reporting workflows.

Ideal Candidate

  • You are someone who genuinely enjoys analysing dataRather than spending your day in meetings,
  • You enjoy solving problems, working through detailed information and producing accurate report.
  • You are naturally organized, methodical and take pride in delivering high-quality work.
  • You enjoy building repeatable processes and finding smarter ways to complete manual tasks.

Initial Projects

  • The successful candidate will initially support projects involving:
  • Carbon footprint calculations
  • Carbon reporting
  • Carbon Reduction Plans
  • Sustainability reporting
  • Utility bill analysis
  • Energy consumption analysis
  • Emissions data collection
  • Client reporting
  • Spreadsheet modelling
  • Data quality assurance
  • Future Growth
  • As the business grows, the role is expected to expand into:
  • Sustainability Consulting Support
  • Carbon Accounting
  • ESG Reporting
  • Compliance Support
  • Client Reporting
  • Environmental Data Analysis
  • AI-assisted Sustainability Reporting
  • Process Automation
  • Proposal Support

The successful candidate will become a key part of the consultancy, helping deliver accurate carbon reporting while enabling the business to scale by taking ownership of the technical analysis and reporting work.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary based on experience and skill set
  • 100% remote role — work from home anywhere in the Philippines
  • Paid local holidays aligned with the Australian business calendar
  • Opportunities for training and professional growth
  • Work directly with a supportive Australian team — no agency middleman
  • Long-term engagement with a stable and growing business

About Anthesis:
Anthesis is the sustainability activator. Proud to be a B Corp, we seek to make a significant contribution to a world which is more resilient and productive. We do this by working with cities, corporates, investors and other organisations to drive sustainable performance. We develop financially driven sustainability strategies, underpinned by technical expertise and delivered by innovative collaborative teams across the world.

At Anthesis Group, we are truly committed to putting people and our planet at the heart of all we do.

Key Responsibilities

We are seeking a Business Development Lead to join our Carbon & Energy Markets Service Line. The Carbon & Energy Markets team at Anthesis partners with organizations to accelerate their decarbonization strategies by providing market-leading expertise in voluntary carbon markets, renewable energy certificates (RECs/EACs), and other sustainability solutions.

This role is responsible for developing new business opportunities, managing strategic client relationships, and leading commercial transactions involving environmental commodities. Working with a diverse portfolio of clients, from multinational corporations to emerging organizations, you will leverage your market expertise, commercial acumen, and consultative approach to help clients achieve their climate and sustainability goals while contributing to the continued growth of Anthesis' Carbon & Energy Markets business.
  • Develop and execute business development strategies to grow Anthesis Carbon & Energy Markets portfolio across North America.
  • Identify, engage, and secure new clients interested in carbon credits, RECs, EACs, PPAs, and other environmental commodities and sustainability solutions.
  • Manage and expand relationships with existing clients, identifying cross-selling and upselling opportunities across Anthesis service lines.
  • Build and maintain a robust pipeline of opportunities through prospecting, networking, industry events, and strategic partnerships.
  • Lead sales processes from opportunity identification through proposal development, negotiation, contracting, and deal closure.
  • Collaborate with internal technical, advisory, and project teams to design tailored solutions that meet clients’ sustainability, decarbonization, and renewable energy goals.
  • Develop relationships with carbon project developers, brokers, traders, utilities, and renewable energy market participants.
  • Support market intelligence activities, monitoring trends, pricing, regulations, and emerging opportunities within carbon and energy attribute markets.
  • Meet or exceed annual revenue, margin, and business development targets while ensuring high levels of client satisfaction.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise

  • 5+ years of experience in business development, account management, environmental commodities, renewable energy, sustainability consulting, or related commercial roles.
  • Proven track record of originating and closing complex sales opportunities with corporate clients and consistently achieving revenue targets.
  • Strong knowledge of voluntary carbon markets, carbon credits, project types, market mechanisms, and corporate climate strategies.
  • Demonstrated experience selling carbon credits, RECs, EACs, and other environmental commodities to corporate buyers.
  • Knowledge of renewable energy procurement solutions and energy markets, including RECs, EACs, PPAs, VPPAs, and related market instruments.
  • Strong existing portfolio of corporate clients and industry contacts within carbon markets, renewable energy, environmental commodities, and sustainability sectors, with a proven track record of generating new revenue opportunities, expanding existing accounts, and securing new client relationships.
  • Demonstrated ability to leverage professional networks to originate opportunities, build a qualified pipeline, and close new business.
  • Proven experience using HubSpot (or similar CRM platforms) to manage sales pipelines, track opportunities, forecast revenue, monitor client activity, and support business development efforts.
  • Strong consultative selling skills, with the ability to translate sustainability and decarbonization objectives into commercial solutions for clients.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to work independently, identify opportunities, and drive business growth.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and pipeline management skills.
  • Willingness to travel periodically for client meetings, conferences, and industry events.
  • Spanish is considered a plus.

Job Benefits

  • Comprehensive and competitive group health, dental, and vision insurance plans for you and your dependents
  • FSA (Flexible Spending Account) benefit (US only)
  • Anthesis provides 100% Basic and Voluntary Life Insurance and Accidental Death and Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance benefit.
  • In addition, Anthesis covers 100% of Short & Long‐Term Disability Insurance benefits.
  • Anthesis provides a 3% contribution into retirement plans, and you may elect to contribute more each pay period with a pre‐tax deduction up to a certain cap.
  • Anthesis provides Employee Assistance Program and Travel Insurance
  • Annual allotment of PTO, in addition to 56 hours of sick leave, paid company paid holidays, and more.
  • Work within a highly motivated team in an innovative and rapidly growing global company.
  • Opportunity to have a direct impact and be a key part of the growth and development of the business and the team.
  • Work collaboratively on projects that have an impact on the sustainability and climate change goals/challenges for clients.
  • Opportunity to work alongside of, collaborate with and learn from sustainability Subject Matter Experts (SME) who are passionate about the work they do and the impact Anthesis can have.

Position: Sustainability Consultant

Salary: € 1400 - € 1600
Working Hours & Conditions: 9:00am – 5:30pm, UK time; full-time (remote)

Holidays: TBD

ROLE OVERVIEW:

We are seeking a Sustainability Consultant to lead on carbon footprint calculations, produce clear and accurate client-facing reports, and provide actionable recommendations to help firms reduce their environmental impact. This is a client-facing role requiring strong technical, analytical, and communication skills.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Collect, verify, and analyse client activity data (energy use, travel, waste, procurement, etc.) to calculate organisational carbon footprints (Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions)
  • Apply recognised methodologies and standards (e.g. GHG Protocol, ISO 14064, SECR, PAS 2060) to ensure calculations are accurate and defensible
  • Produce clear, well-structured carbon footprint reports suitable for client boards, investors, or regulatory submission
  • Translate technical findings into practical, prioritised recommendations for emissions reduction tailored to each client's sector and operations
  • Support clients with target-setting (e.g. Science Based Targets) and net zero roadmaps
  • Stay current with UK and international sustainability regulations, reporting frameworks, and best practice
  • Liaise directly with clients to gather data, present findings, and answer queries
  • Manage multiple client projects concurrently, meeting agreed deadlines
  • Contribute to internal tools, templates, and calculation methodologies to improve efficiency and consistency

Requirements

  • Proven experience calculating carbon footprints using the GHG Protocol or equivalent methodology
  • Strong Excel/data analysis skills; experience with carbon accounting software (e.g. SINAI, Watershed, Normative, or similar) advantageous
  • Excellent written communication skills, with demonstrable experience producing professional reports
  • Ability to translate complex technical data into clear recommendations for non-technical audiences
  • Strong attention to detail and comfort working with large datasets
  • Good working knowledge of UK sustainability regulation and reporting requirements (e.g. SECR, TCFD, CSRD if working with EU-linked clients)

We are CBAM Estimator, a young SaaS company based in Stuttgart. Our mission is to help companies meet the requirements of the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) accurately, efficiently and at scale.

We build modern web platforms that help international manufacturing and trading companies calculate emissions, manage CBAM-related data and prepare the documentation required for CBAM compliance.

We are an international team with diverse backgrounds spanning emissions accounting, environmental science, IT, mathematics and business. We share a commitment to making complex regulatory requirements manageable through a pragmatic and transparent approach.

To support our work with manufacturers in China, we are looking for an Environmental Engineer / Carbon Specialist based in China who combines technical expertise in environmental matters with strong communication skills.

You will work directly with Chinese manufacturers, helping them understand CBAM data requirements, collect the necessary emissions and production data, and prepare supporting documentation. You will also act as a bridge between local manufacturers and our international team.

You do not need to be a CBAM expert from day one. A strong technical background in environmental engineering, carbon accounting, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions or a related field is more important. We will help you develop the necessary CBAM expertise.

Tasks

  • Support Chinese manufacturers in collecting and organising emissions and production data
  • Help manufacturers understand the technical and data requirements relevant to CBAM
  • Review GHG emissions, energy and production data to identify missing or inconsistent information
  • Support the calculation and documentation of embedded emissions of goods using relevant installation and production process data in accordance with CBAM requirements
  • Conduct workshops and training sessions for manufacturers
  • Help manufacturers prepare emissions data and supporting documentation for independent third-party verification
  • Support manufacturers in addressing questions and closing data gaps during reporting and verification
  • Work closely with our emissions and product teams in Europe
  • Gather feedback from manufacturers to help us continuously improve our processes, methodology and software

Requirements

Required

  • A degree in environmental engineering, environmental science or a comparable technical field
  • Practical experience working with environmental, energy, emissions or sustainability-related data
  • A good understanding of industrial processes and confidence working with technical teams
  • Excellent written and spoken Mandarin
  • Very good written and spoken English
  • Confidence working with data, spreadsheets, calculations and technical documentation
  • The ability to explain complex technical topics clearly to customers
  • An independent, structured and reliable approach to work

Nice to Have

  • Experience with GHG accounting or corporate or product carbon footprints
  • Knowledge of ISO 14064 and/or ISO 14067
  • Experience with emissions auditing, verification, monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV), or environmental audits
  • Experience delivering workshops or technical training
  • Knowledge of CBAM and/or the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)
  • Experience with industrial processes in the iron and steel, aluminium, cement or fertiliser sectors, or other energy-intensive industries
  • Experience working with international or European customers
  • Experience with life cycle assessment (LCA) or product carbon footprint calculations

Benefits

  • A remote-first working environment for a role based in China
  • Practical experience working directly with industrial manufacturers and international customers
  • The opportunity to develop deep expertise in CBAM, carbon accounting and industrial emissions
  • Close collaboration with our emissions experts and product team
  • Structured onboarding to help you develop CBAM expertise from day one
  • Responsibility from an early stage and the opportunity to shape how we support manufacturers in China
  • An international team working at the intersection of climate regulation, industry and technology
  • A lean working environment with minimal bureaucracy, where your work has a direct impact

Equal Opportunity

CBAM Estimator is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will be considered regardless of race, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability or any other protected characteristic.

Forests are crucial to all life on Earth. They capture and store carbon and are one of the most promising, large-scale, and cost-effective opportunities to combat climate change. Rainforests also sustain rainfalls, food supply, vital ecosystems, and livelihoods for over a billion people. Protecting them is not just a moral imperative, it is essential for a stable, prosperous, and sustainable future for us all. As the COVID-19 crisis highlights, we live in a fragile and interconnected world where sustainability cannot be taken for granted.

There is increasing recognition of the urgency of climate change. The Paris Agreement in 2015 committed governments to keep the increase in global average temperature to well below 2 °C above pre-industrial levels. 760 major corporations have committed to climate neutrality, and over 40 countries have implemented some form of carbon pricing scheme. After two decades of putting necessary, effective, high integrity standards and market mechanisms in place, The Emergent Forest Finance Accelerator (“Emergent”) has the historic opportunity to channel this momentum to solving the deforestation crisis.

Emergent helps safeguard the world’s tropical forests by building a global market for forest carbon credits. Countries generate these credits by reducing deforestation and tropical deforestation (called “REDD+”). For forest countries, Emergent provides a guaranteed source of demand by facilitating access to a range of high-volume buyers, backed by a purchase guarantee from donors, giving countries the certainty need-ed to make investments in forest protection and chart a new course. For buyers, Emergent provides access to the highest-quality REDD+ credits, enabling them to meet their climate neutrality goals.

In the case of corporate purchases of credits, Emergent contracts via a standard ERPA with corporate buyers on a forward, unit-contingent basis. Credits purchased from jurisdictions (also via ERPA) are sold to buyers, with the resulting revenues transferred, minus a small transaction fee, to jurisdictions via UN/World Bank-accredited ‘financial intermediaries’ (FIs). FIs will be contracted by Emergent to provide these transfer services, and to work with jurisdictions to report on the use of the funds for pre-agreed purposes.

In the case of price guarantee purchases, Emergent transfers funding from OECD governments to jurisdictions in return for credits which are then retired. (As well as providing a demand signal to jurisdictions, these transactions are effectively government-to-government ‘results-based payments’ for progress in reducing deforestation.) Before use, these funds may be held by Emergent or potentially in a trust fund arrangement administered by a multilateral such as the UN.

Forests are crucial to all life on Earth. They capture and store carbon and are one of the most promising, large-scale, and cost-effective opportunities to combat climate change. Rainforests also sustain rainfalls, food supply, vital ecosystems, and livelihoods for over a billion people. Protecting them is not just a moral imperative, it is essential for a stable, prosperous, and sustainable future for us all. As the COVID-19 crisis highlights, we live in a fragile and interconnected world where sustainability cannot be taken for granted.

There is increasing recognition of the urgency of climate change. The Paris Agreement in 2015 committed governments to keep the increase in global average temperature to well below 2 °C above pre-industrial levels. Over 1,500 major corporations have committed to climate neutrality, and over 40 countries have implemented some form of carbon pricing scheme. After two decades of putting necessary, effective, high integrity standards and market mechanisms in place, Emergent has the historic opportunity to channel this momentum to solving the deforestation crisis.

Emergent helps safeguard the world’s tropical forests by building a global market for forest carbon credits. Countries generate these credits by reducing deforestation and tropical deforestation (called “REDD+”). For forest countries, Emergent provides a guaranteed source of demand by facilitating access to a range of high-volume buyers, backed by a purchase guarantee from donors, giving countries the certainty need-ed to make investments in forest protection and chart a new course. For buyers, Emergent provides access to the highest-quality REDD+ credits, enabling them to meet their climate neutrality goals.
